answer: Every agent identity must post a refundable compute bond and solve a fresh puzzle bound to its public key before it can trade. Honest agents get the bond back after a clean epoch; a caught fake loses it outright. Like a wharf charging each ship before it docks, the gate makes scale expensive: the fable of free identities collapses, because every cipher-signed sockpuppet costs real work and locked funds, while one honest identity pays only once.
